extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and specialists studying Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and explains the structural properties, compatibility/indeterminacy constraints, and required hypotheses used in the logical apparatus of inter-universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory (Θ-links, log-links, log-theta-lattice, pilot objects, indeterminacies). Intended for readers analyzing or applying the formal structure of IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θk non-symmetric with respect to switching domain/codomain (ii-a)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The isomorphism Θk : FN ∼→ F1 is not symmetric with respect to switching the domain/codomain in the following sense: there do not exist Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms φ : k → k, ψ : k → k such that the induced maps ... fit into a diagram ... that is commutative on the portion of the diagram on which the relevant composites are defined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text justifies this by tracing images at the level of value groups: certain elements map to q under one composite but to qN^2 (≡ qN) via another, hence no symmetric Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms making the diagram commute exist. Use value-group tracing to detect such non-symmetricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: logk non-symmetric with respect to switching domain/codomain (ii-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The isomorphism logk : O×_k ∼→ k is not symmetric with respect to switching the domain/codomain in the following sense: there do not exist Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms φ : k → k, ψ : k → k that fit into a diagram ... that is commutative on the portion of the diagram on which the relevant composites are defined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument parallels (ii-a): follow specific elements (e.g., u = {exp(p^2)^{1/p^2}} ∈ O×_k) through the proposed commutative squares to see differing images, showing absence of symmetric equivariant maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological-group action diagram symmetric only after applying coricity properties (ii-c)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The topological group actions surrounding Θk yield a diagram that is [manifestly!] symmetric with respect to applying the operation of ‘reflection’ ... this symmetry property only holds if the coricity properties discussed in (i-e), (i-f) are applied, i.e., if the isomorphism of topological groups Gk ∼→ Gk is regarded as an indeterminate isomorphism of abstract topological groups and the arrows ‘(cid:4)/(cid:5)’ are regarded as surjections between abstract topological groups ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recover the symmetry one must treat Gk-isomorphisms as indeterminate and regard arrows as surjections of abstract topological groups; failing to apply coricity yields structures depending on domain/codomain-specific Galois-rigidifications and symmetry breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θk does not commute with logk (iii-a)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Θk does not commute with logk — i.e., at a purely formal level, ‘Θk ◦ logk ≠ logk ◦ Θk’ — in the following sense: there do not exist Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms φ : k → k, ψ : k → k such that the induced maps ... fit into a diagram ... that is commutative on the portion of the diagram on which the relevant composites are defined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrated by tracing a carefully chosen element (e.g., certain exp(p^n·N) units) through the two composites and observing different images in the value group; use these explicit traces to certify non-commutativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θk not invariant with respect to logk (iii-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Θk is not invariant with respect to logk — i.e., at a purely formal level, ‘Θk ◦ logk ≠ Θk’ — in the following sense: there do not exist Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms φ : k → k, ψ : k → k such that the induced maps ... fit into a diagram ... that is commutative on the portion of the diagram on which the relevant composites are defined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar tracing argument as (iii-a): pick integers n sufficiently large relative to p-adic denominators, trace the element un = exp(p^n·N) and compare images along different composites to see failure of invariance. The construction relies on control of p-adic valuation ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatibility with ring structures of Θ-link/log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: “the incompatibility with the ring structures in the domain/codomain ... of the Θ-link and log-link” (bullet in §3.2→§3.3 summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Θ- and log-links deform/juggle multiplicative and additive structures in ways incompatible with a naïve identification of full ring structures across domain and codomain; careful separation of unit- and value-group splittings is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity: horizontal and vertical coricity properties of étale-like structures
rubrics_metrics.description: “the horizontal ... and vertical ... coricity properties of the ´etale-like structures that appear in the log-theta-lattice” (summary bullets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The log-theta-lattice requires treating certain étale-like structures with coricity (i.e., considered only up to indeterminate isomorphism) to obtain the intended symmetry/compatibility properties; this affects how group actions and maps are interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-symmetricity of Θ-link/log-link under domain/codomain switch
rubrics_metrics.description: “the non-symmetricity with respect to switching the domain/codomain ... of the Θ-link ... and log-link” (summary bullets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One must not assume natural symmetry between domain and codomain; explicit counterexamples are given by tracing value-group images and unit permutations that differ under different compositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetricity (under conditions) of étale-like structures with respect to Θ-link
rubrics_metrics.description: “the symmetricity with respect to the Θ-link ... of the ´etale-like structures of the log-theta-lattice” (summary bullets; referenced (ii-c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symmetricity can be recovered only after treating certain structures as indeterminate and applying coricity properties; this is essential for parts of the logical structure that depend on symmetric group-action diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-commutativity of the log-theta-lattice
rubrics_metrics.description: “the non-commutativity of the log-theta-lattice” (summary bullets; referenced (iii-a) and §3.3 introduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect diagrams in the log-theta-lattice to fail to commute in controlled ways; such non-commutativity is measured and exploited in later constructions (e.g., in computing log-volumes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-invariance of Θ-link with respect to log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: “the non-invariance of the Θ-link with respect to the log-link” (summary bullets; referenced (iii-b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Θ and log operations do not preserve one another; proofs analyze explicit elements and their differing images under compositions, and this non-invariance is part of the structural toolkit rather than a pathology to be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid identification of domain and codomain of log-link (falsity of RC-log)
rubrics_metrics.description: “there is no natural way to relate the two Θ-links ... that emanate from the domain and codomain of the log-link ... there is no natural candidate for ‘??’ ... that makes the diagram commute ... any identification of the domain and codomain of the log-link ... yields a situation in which the local splittings into unit groups and value groups of the resulting identified ‘•’s are no longer well-defined. In particular, any such identification ... yields a situation in which the Θ-link is not well-defined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not identify domain/codomain of log-links (RC-log). Such identifications destroy the unit/value group splittings fundamental to defining Θ-links and therefore break the entire apparatus; arguments use analogies to dilations and multiplication by roots of unity to justify this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompatibility of dilations with multiplication by non-real roots of unity (classical analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example 3.3.1: “Λ is not compatible with multiplication by μn unless n = 2 ... This incompatibility ... is one fundamental reason for the special role played by square differentials ... in classical complex Teichmüller theory.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogize to classical Teichmüller dilations: when applying dilation-type maps, multiplication by nth roots of unity (n≥3) breaks compatibility; this analogy motivates restrictions (e.g., focusing on squares) in the IUT setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Jacobi identity / ι-invariance to relate difficult asymptotics
rubrics_metrics.description: Example 3.3.2: Jacobi identity θ(t) = t^{-1/2}·θ(t^{-1}) provides an invariance with respect to ι (t ↦ t^{-1}) up to an explicit factor t^{-1/2}, allowing analysis of θ(t) as t→0 via t→∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ identities like the Jacobi identity (and underlying Fourier transform invariance of the Gaussian) to convert hard asymptotic computations into tractable ones; in IUT this plays an analogous role to log-link invariance and multiradial constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressibility of theta-function properties purely multiplicatively (ThMlt)
rubrics_metrics.description: “the main properties of interest of the theta functions ... — most notably, (ZrPl) the description of zeroes/poles at the cusps, (SymTh) the well-known symmetries of theta functions, (GalEv) the Kummer-compatible Galois evaluation properties — may be expressed entirely in terms of the multiplicative structures of the various rings that appear, i.e., without invoking the additive structures of these rings.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplicative expressibility is foundational: it enables multiradial unit/value-group splittings and non-interference properties used to define Θ-links and log-Kummer correspondences; when applicable, prefer multiplicative formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeros/poles of theta functions at cusps have signed order one (ZrPlOrd)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(ZrPlOrd) the signed order [i.e., ‘+’ for zeroes, ‘−’ for poles] of the theta function at each of the cusps is precisely one.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property ensures cyclotomic rigidity algorithms coming from theta functions are compatible with the topology of the tempered fundamental group and are not subject to {±1}-indeterminacies; it is critical in arguments relying on mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicative-to-additive reconstruction holds for algebraic rational functions (MltAdd) but not for theta functions
rubrics_metrics.description: “(MltAdd) the anabelian reconstruction algorithms ... imply that the additive structure of the function field of an algebraic curve may in fact be reconstructed from the multiplicative structure ... once one allows oneself to work with algebraic rational functions ... By contrast, if one restricts oneself ... to considering theta functions ... then (MltAdd) is no longer applicable ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume multiplicative-only descriptions suffice when working with algebraic rational functions (MltAdd applies there), but recognize theta-function contexts where multiplicative expressibility remains genuinely stronger and distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrepancies in vertical lines quantified by indeterminacy (Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.description: “the discrepancy between the [holomorphic] Frobenius-like copies of objects on either side of a log-link ... and the discrepancy between [holomorphic] Frobenius-like copies of objects and [holomorphic] étale-like copies of objects ... may be understood as the extent to which the diagram ... fails to commute. This failure to commute may be estimated by means of the indeterminacy (Ind3) ... gives rise to the inequality that appears in the final computation of log-volumes ... the theory ... depends ... on the absolute anabelian geometry ... which allows one to reconstruct ... a hyperbolic curve ... from the abstract profinite group ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat (Ind3) as a quantitative control on ‘upper semi-commutativity’; use absolute anabelian geometry to bound these discrepancies (they are nontrivial but controlled), and these bounds feed into log-volume inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Θ-link gluing uses full poly-isomorphism of F×μ-prime-strips; pilots (Θ-plt, q-plt) differ
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Θ-link ... is defined ... as a gluing ... along F×μ-prime-strips ‘∗’ that arise from the Θ-pilot object ‘Θ-plt’ in the domain and the q-pilot object ‘q-plt’ in the codomain. ... Note that since, for j ≠ 1, the valuation ... of q_j^{2} differs from that of q, the arithmetic degrees of the line bundles constituted by q-plt and Θ-plt differ.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gluing is performed by taking the full set of isomorphisms (poly-isomorphism) between the prime-strips; keep pilot objects distinct and track differing arithmetic degrees — these differences are essential to the logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of distinct labels (†, ‡) to guarantee the AND relator (AOΘ1)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(AOΘ1) the following condition holds: ∗ :→ †Θ-plt ∈ †Ring ∧ ∗ :→ ‡q-plt ∈ ‡Ring. By contrast, if one simply deletes the distinct labels ‘†’, ‘‡’ (RC-Θ)!, then (AOΘ2) ... ∗ :→ Θ-plt ∈ Ring ∨ ∗ :→ q-plt ∈ Ring.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining distinct domain/codomain labels (†, ‡) ensures both pilot assignments hold simultaneously (AND). Deleting the labels collapses the AND into an OR and destroys the structural content required for IUT constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminating distinct labels converts AND into OR and destroys required structure (AOΘ2–AOΘ4)
rubrics_metrics.description: “(AOΘ2) ... ∗ :→ Θ-plt ∈ Ring ∨ ∗ :→ q-plt ∈ Ring. ... (AOΘ4) the following condition does not hold: ∗ :→ Θ-plt ∈ Ring ∧ ∗ :→ q-plt ∈ Ring. That is to say, identifying †•, ‡• ... has the effect of passing from a situation in which the AND relator ‘∧’ holds ... to one in which the OR relator ‘∨’ holds ... but the AND relator ‘∧’ does not hold.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid neutralizing labels: such identification forces a loss of simultaneous pilot assignments; proofs relying on both assignments (AND) fail, so the labeling distinction is indispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoRng: nonexistence of a ring isomorphism inducing desired value-group assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: “(NoRng) there does not exist an isomorphism of ring structures †Ring ∼→ ‡Ring that induces, on value groups of corresponding local rings, the desired assignment {†q_j^{2}_v} → ‡q_v.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One cannot circumvent labeling issues by producing a global ring isomorphism that matches the required pilot-value assignments; any purported neutral ring must confront this obstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with multiplicative monoids + abstract topological groups yields simultaneity and indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2)
rubrics_metrics.description: “if ... one considers certain suitable subquotients — of the underlying multiplicative monoids of corresponding local fields, as well as the absolute Galois groups ... then one obtains structures ... that are simultaneously associated ... to both †Ring and ‡Ring via isomorphisms ... It is this crucial simultaneity that yields ... the validity of the AND relator ‘∧’ ... Working ... with multiplicative monoids equipped with actions by abstract topological groups, necessarily gives rise to certain indeterminacies, called (Ind1), (Ind2) ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept and manage (Ind1), (Ind2): they are milder indeterminacies that arise from working with subquotient multiplicative structures and abstract topological groups, but they enable the simultaneity needed for AOΘ1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral-ring approach (NeuRng / NeuORInd) causes drastic OR-type indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: “(NeuRng) these indeterminacies (Ind1), (Ind2) may be eliminated ... by taking ... a fixed ‘neutral’ ring structure (cid:6)Ring. On the other hand, ... there does not exist any ring structure that is compatible ... with the desired assignment ... (NeuORInd) working with such a fixed ‘neutral’ ring structure ... means either that (NeuORInd1) there is no relationship between ‘∗’ and (cid:6)Ring, or that (NeuORInd2) the relationship between ‘∗’ and (cid:6)Ring is always necessarily subject to an indeterminacy ... this much more drastic indeterminacy (NeuORInd) means ... that the only possible relationship between ‘∗’ and (cid:6)Θ-plt, (cid:6)q-plt is one in which (PltRel) ‘∗’ maps either to (cid:6)Θ-plt or — i.e., ‘∨’! — to (cid:6)q-plt, but not both! ... (RngRel) the ring structure (cid:6)Ring is identified either with the ring structure ‡Ring or ... with the ring structure †Ring, but not both!”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposing a neutral ring produces a severe (NeuORInd) OR-indeterminacy: the neutralization forces exclusivity (∗ maps to only one pilot), making the IUT apparatus nonfunctional. Therefore, neutral-ring rigidification is not an acceptable simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: IUT requires log-links and ring structures on both sides of Θ-link (AND), impossible under NeuORInd
rubrics_metrics.description: “inter-universal Teichmüller theory requires, in an essential way, the use of the log-links, hence, in particular, [in order to define the power series ...] the ring structures †Ring, ‡Ring on both sides — i.e., ‘∧’! — of the Θ-link ... it is impossible to implement the arguments of inter-universal Teichmüller theory once this sort of much more drastic indeterminacy (NeuORInd) has been imposed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain both ring structures and their coexistence (AND). Many core constructions (log power series, multiradial representations) break if one attempts to collapse to a single neutral ring; proofs must rely on both sides being present.
